name: CCapture.js
role: Fixed-framerate canvas capture by hooking browser time; 2.x rewrite on WebCodecs
summary: Browser library that overrides timing functions (Date, requestAnimationFrame, optionally performance.now) so a canvas animation advances one fixed step per captured frame, then writes MP4/WebM via WebCodecs, GIF via gifenc, or PNG/JPG/WebP frames in a tar. 2.0.0 is a ground-up rewrite adding GPU motion blur. Distinguishing strength: retrofits deterministic capture onto code you cannot change to render on demand.
use_when: Existing canvas animation driven by rAF or Date that you cannot refactor to seek
Motion blur by sub-frame sampling on a canvas or WebGL scene, in-browser
Over canvas-record when time-hooking an unmodified sketch beats refactoring it
avoid_when: Web Audio, CSS animations or WAAPI: not frame-stepped; Playwright with beginFrame covers them
Seekable timelines such as GSAP: Playwright seeks them exactly, no time hooking
Server-side or CI capture: Playwright frames into FFmpeg
notes: 2026-10-26: PRD flagged this as unmaintained; that is outdated, 2.0.0 shipped 2026-07-27 as a rewrite. Single-maintainer project; the 1.x API was removed, so older tutorials do not apply.
2026-10-26: time hooking (hookDate) is global and breaks real date arithmetic during capture; not exercised.

assessment.rationale: PRD called it unmaintained but v2.0.0, a WebCodecs rewrite, was published 2026-07-27 and the repo was pushed 2026-10-13. 1.x API removed. Time-hooking is the niche; Playwright is the validated route.
